stem:
Ritu adds vegetable peels and cow dung to a closed pit. After a few weeks the waste has turned into dark, nutrient-rich manure. Bacteria, fungi, and viruses can be found in soil.

Which statement best explains the change?

options.text: Bacteria and fungi break the plant and animal waste down into simpler, nutrient-rich manure.
The waste becomes manure on its own, and then microorganisms arrive to feed on it.
Viruses in the soil break the waste down into nutrient-rich manure.
Fresh peels that look dark are already nutrient-rich manure.

teacher.key_rationale: Soil bacteria and fungi decompose plant and animal waste into manure. Manure does not form first and then attract microbes; viruses are not the decomposers here; dark colour alone does not mean finished manure.
